newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades steady at 3.00/3.05 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades steady at 3.00/3.05 pct.

text.p: German call money traded unchanged at 3.00/3.05 percent on Thursday with the bulk of deals conducted between 3.02/3.03, dealers said.

While overnight rates were mostly steady, dealers said the market was not totally in equilibrium. Banks' reserve holdings, standing at 39 billion marks, were not overly ample but there were signs these would rise in coming sessions.
"We can live with the reserve requirements at the moment," one dealer said, adding that it was still early in the month.
Another dealer added that there was not need to get overly worried about the situation at this time in the month.
Dealers said that the Bundesbank must have known about extra liquidity which justified Wednesday's unexpectedly high money market liquidity drain.
Bank holdings stood at 39 billion marks on Wednesday with average holdings standing at 38.1 billion marks. Meanwhile Lombard borrowings were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.04733 percent on Thursday compared with 3.05933 percent on Wednesday.
